chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the intermarriage (or cohabitation/marriage by choice) of the Magian woman, so he said: 'No, but [it is for] the People of the Book.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَاب: People of the Book (typically Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: Is a Muslim man allowed to marry a Zoroastrian (Magian) woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific scope of Quranic permission for Muslim men to marry chaste women from the People of the Book, explicitly excluding the Magians (Zoroastrians) who are not considered 'People of the Book' in this legal context. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that the term 'Ahl al-Kitab' refers strictly to Jews and Christians, thereby limiting the permissibility of intermarriage to these two groups alone.
